label: Village
_model: The settlement kernel at its smallest. The appetite belongs to the place; the claimant is an office, not a person; and what a village does to people who might leave is quieter and worse than what a town does.

appetites.purpose: every name would stay on the register

appeasement.move: say a name off the register aloud, correctly, as though they were still here

appetites.purpose: the harvest would always come in

appeasement.move: give something of your own to the store, and enough of it

appetites.want: that nothing here should ever alter
appetites.purpose: it would be the same place forever

appeasement.move: do one thing exactly the way it has always been done here

appetites.want: that nothing here should ever be spoken of outside

appeasement.move: agree, out loud, that you saw nothing

accommodations.text: married {conscript} in so that they could not leave
gave {conscript} a strip of the common they could never sell
entered {conscript} in the register under a name that was not theirs
buried something of {conscript}'s under the boundary stone
held {conscript} back each harvest until there was no season left to go
agreed, all of them, never to speak of {conscript} again

register.label: the parish register, every name in one hand
register.function: the only complete account of who was ever here

sheaf.label: the last sheaf of the last good harvest
sheaf.function: the only year the store was full

stone.label: the boundary stone, small enough to carry
stone.function: the only thing that says where this place stops

book.label: the book nobody has read since it was written
book.function: the only place the thing was written down

factions.name: the Parish
factions.essence: still counted, still on the register, still expected at church

factions.name: the hungry year
factions.essence: came for the store and stayed when the village did not

factions.name: those who keep the custom
factions.essence: will not be told this is not how it is done

factions.name: what came off the common
factions.essence: was never entered on any roll

triggerGlossary.announced: walked in down the lane, in daylight, and were seen doing it
triggerGlossary.seenTwice: noticed by the same person twice in one day
triggerGlossary.loud: a raised voice anywhere within the sound of the church
triggerGlossary.lingering: stopped somewhere long enough for it to be remarked on
triggerGlossary.disturbed: moved a boundary, opened a gate, or took something off the common

foes.name: Bandit
foes.note: local; will run for the ditches

skirmish.avoid: they want the store, not you; leave the store and they leave you

fight.line: 4 Skeletons of the Parish and a Ghoul in the pest house

foes.name: Ghoul
foes.note: free Called Shot to freeze on a hit

fight.avoid: the Parish does not leave consecrated ground; step off it and they stop

battle.line: 1 Wraith of the Reeve and 4 Skeletons of the Parish

foes.name: Wraith
foes.note: INCORPOREAL — chill touch ignores armour, drains 1 max Grit

battle.harmedBy: blessed, silvered or magical weapons for the Wraith ONLY; anything for the Skeletons
battle.avoid: it wants the count right; give it a name off the register and it stops to check

nightmare.line: 1 Wraith, 1 Ogre off the common and 5 Skeletons

foes.name: Ogre
foes.note: came off the common and was never entered anywhere

nightmare.harmedBy: blessed, silvered or magical weapons for the Wraith ONLY; anything for the rest
nightmare.avoid: do not run this without an appeasement route open

kinship.dangerLine: the parish is still counting, and it is short

institution: a register with every family in the same hand for two hundred years
cottages built onto other cottages as the families grew
ritual: names read out at the door before the service
a place laid for somebody at every table
the roll called on the green each quarter-day
demand: a gap in a row of names with the ruling still drawn
a chair kept back from a table that is otherwise full
a cottage kept swept for somebody
wound: a page torn out of the register and the stub still in
a pew with the name planed off
cottages standing open with the beds still made
anchor: the register, every name in one hand
a family bible with the births still being entered
a tally of the village cut into a beam

features: a place laid at a table for nobody
a pew with a name planed off
a cottage swept and empty
a torn stub in a register
a name read out at a door
a chair kept back from the table

decisions.cue: a register with a gap in the names and the ruling still drawn
decisions.cost: filling it enters somebody on the roll for good

resolve.success: you enter a name that satisfies the count and the Parish stops looking at you
resolve.failure: you enter one of your own and the village considers them settled here: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave the gap; the Parish keeps counting, and keeps coming back to you

decisions.cue: a place laid at a table for somebody who is not coming
decisions.cost: sitting in it accepts the place

resolve.success: you sit, eat, and are treated as family — every door in the village opens
resolve.failure: you sit and cannot rise until somebody else takes the place
resolve.orElse: stay standing; you are guests, and guests are watched

decisions.cue: a pew with the name planed off and the wood pale
decisions.cost: the name is recoverable from the register

resolve.success: you match the pew to {priorCue} and learn who the village will not name
resolve.failure: you say the name aloud in the church and something answers to it
resolve.orElse: leave it blank; you never learn who this was

decisions.cue: cottages standing open with the beds still made
decisions.cost: somebody could be housed here tonight

resolve.success: you make the cottage yours for the night and the Parish leaves you be until morning
resolve.failure: you sleep and wake counted — the Parish now expects you at everything
resolve.orElse: sleep outside the village; you lose the night and gain a Turn of pressure

decisions.cue: a tally of the village cut into a beam, one notch short
decisions.cost: cutting a notch is a claim; shaving one is a lie

resolve.success: you shave a notch and the Parish believes the count already right
resolve.failure: you cut one and are the notch: the village treats you as resident
resolve.orElse: leave the beam; the shortfall keeps drawing the Parish to the living

decisions.cue: a family bible with the births still being entered in fresh ink
decisions.cost: somebody is still writing

resolve.success: you find who is writing, and they will tell you who is missing and why
resolve.failure: you write in it, and the ink takes: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: close it; the entries continue without you

situations.occupant: an old woman of the Parish
situations.doing: laying a place at a table that is otherwise full
situations.onArrival: she asks whether you are the one they sent for
situations.because: the place has been laid every night since somebody left
situations.offer: sit in the place and she will tell you every name the village has lost

situations.doing: calling a roll on the green to nobody
situations.onArrival: they pause at a gap and look at you
situations.because: the roll must be got through and one name has no answer
situations.offer: answer to the name and the whole village receives you as its own

situations.doing: counting cottages, out loud, and getting a different number twice
situations.onArrival: it starts again when it sees you
situations.because: the count has never come right since
situations.offer: give it a number it can accept and it will unlock the church

situations.doing: sorting through goods nobody came out to buy
situations.onArrival: they ask, quietly, whether the village has always been like this
situations.because: they came in this morning and cannot find the way back out
situations.offer: tell them the truth and they will show you the lane they came in by

situations.doing: waiting at a gate with a bundle packed
situations.onArrival: it asks whether you are going, and whether it may come
situations.because: it was told to be ready and nobody came for it
situations.offer: take the bundle and it will lead you anywhere in the parish

situations.doing: standing at their doors, not coming out
situations.onArrival: every head turns to follow you down the lane
situations.because: strangers are counted before they are spoken to
situations.offer: greet one by name, correctly, and the doors open

temptations.cue: a leaf out of the parish register
temptations.benefit: once, be who a name on it was
temptations.standingDrawback: the Parish expects that person's obligations of you

temptations.cue: a family bible with the births in fresh ink
temptations.benefit: know who belongs to whom, everywhere here
temptations.standingDrawback: you are entered in it too

temptations.cue: a piece cut from the tally beam
temptations.benefit: once, be counted as one of the village
temptations.standingDrawback: one of yours goes uncounted while you hold it

temptations.cue: a keepsake left in an empty cottage
temptations.benefit: once, the Parish takes you for the one who left
temptations.standingDrawback: whoever left is still owed something

temptations.cue: a packed bundle nobody came back for
temptations.benefit: once, leave anywhere unhindered
temptations.standingDrawback: you are leaving in somebody else's place

harvest.dangerLine: the store is empty and the village has not stopped filling it

institution: a tithe barn bigger than the church
strips of the common apportioned by a rule nobody wrote down
a store-book listing what each household owes in
ritual: the last sheaf cut and hung in the rafters
a portion set aside at every meal and not eaten
the store counted each week whether anything went in or not
demand: a scale set out with nothing on either pan
a barn door standing open onto empty boards
a sack held ready by somebody who does not put it down
wound: a barn stripped to the boards and swept clean
the last sheaf gone black in the rafters
a store-book where the entries stop mid-week
anchor: the last sheaf of the last good harvest
a full sack in an empty barn

features: a portion set aside and not eaten
the last sheaf hung black in the rafters
a scale with nothing in either pan
a barn swept to the boards
a sack nobody puts down
a store-book stopping mid-week

decisions.cue: a scale set out with nothing on either pan and the weights beside it
decisions.cost: weighing something in is a contribution

resolve.success: you weigh in enough of your own and the village counts you as having paid your part
resolve.failure: you weigh in short and the shortfall is remembered against you: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: walk past the scale; nothing here will feed you

decisions.cue: the last sheaf hung black in the rafters, still tied
decisions.cost: taking it down ends something

resolve.success: you take it down whole and the store will yield what you ask for once
resolve.failure: it comes apart in your hands and the year goes with it: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: leave it hanging; the barn stays shut to you

decisions.cue: a store-book whose entries stop mid-week in a hurried hand
decisions.cost: the last entry says why

resolve.success: you read the last week and learn what the village did when the store ran out
resolve.failure: you read it aloud and something that was there that week hears you
resolve.orElse: close it; you go on not knowing what they did

decisions.cue: a portion set aside at a table and not eaten
decisions.cost: eating it takes a share; adding to it gives one

resolve.success: you add to the portion and the household spirits attend you for the delve
resolve.failure: you eat it and are hungry for the rest of the delve: -1 die on Brawn
resolve.orElse: leave it; the portion sits there, and is noticed

decisions.cue: a barn door standing open onto swept boards
decisions.cost: closing it says the store is full

resolve.success: you fill enough of the floor to shut the door honestly, and the village rests
resolve.failure: you shut it on nothing and the lie is felt through the whole parish: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it open; every night thing in the parish knows the barn is empty

decisions.cue: strips of the common apportioned by a rule nobody wrote down
decisions.cost: working one claims it

resolve.success: you work out the rule and can take a strip without offending anybody
resolve.failure: you take the wrong strip and the Hayward has you for it
resolve.orElse: take no strip; you have no standing here and doors stay shut

situations.doing: pacing out a strip of the common, over and over
situations.onArrival: it stops and asks whose strip you are standing on
situations.because: the apportionment was never finished
situations.offer: name a household and it will let you pass and tell you what is buried there

situations.doing: carrying an empty sack between them, carefully
situations.onArrival: they set it down in front of you and wait
situations.because: the sack must go to the barn full and never has
situations.offer: put anything at all in the sack and they will carry you anywhere in the parish

situations.doing: running a mill with nothing going through it
situations.onArrival: they ask what you have brought to grind
situations.because: the mill was never stopped and they cannot stop it
situations.offer: give them a handful of anything and they will tell you what the village eats now

situations.doing: counting an empty barn, slowly, by touch
situations.onArrival: it looks up and asks whether the carts have come
situations.because: the count is done each week whether or not there is anything to count
situations.offer: tell it the carts are coming and it will open the barn's inner room

situations.doing: standing in a field that has not been sown
situations.onArrival: its head turns as you cross the furrow
situations.because: it was set to watch the crop and the crop never came
situations.offer: dress it properly and the field lets you cross without being seen

situations.doing: hanging black in the rafters above a swept floor
situations.onArrival: it swings slightly in a barn with no draught
situations.because: it was cut in the last good year and never taken down
situations.offer: cut it down and the store gives up what it has been keeping

temptations.cue: a handful off the last good sheaf
temptations.benefit: once, make a thing sufficient that was not
temptations.standingDrawback: the store is one portion shorter and knows it

temptations.cue: the store-book
temptations.benefit: know what every household here has and owes
temptations.standingDrawback: you are entered as owing too

temptations.cue: a scale weight, heavier than it looks
temptations.benefit: once, make a bargain come out your way
temptations.standingDrawback: the other side always finds out afterwards

temptations.cue: a pocket of seed corn from the sealed sack
temptations.benefit: once, make something grow where it should not
temptations.standingDrawback: it grows, and it keeps growing

temptations.cue: a portion set aside and never eaten
temptations.benefit: once, be fed anywhere
temptations.standingDrawback: you eat what somebody else was owed

custom.dangerLine: there is a way things are done here and it is still being kept

institution: a moot stone with the worn places where feet go
a manor court that has met on the same day for four hundred years
gates hung so they can only be opened in one order
ritual: a procession walked round the bounds each year, in the same direction
a stone turned once a season by whoever is nearest
the same words said at the same gate before anybody passes
demand: a mark on a threshold that expects to be stepped over, not on
a gate standing shut in a fence with no fence either side
a place on the stone where somebody should be standing
wound: the bounds walked backwards, once, and the marks scuffed
a moot stone split and the halves set apart
gates rehung the wrong way round
anchor: the boundary stone, small enough to carry
a court roll listing every custom and its penalty
a staff cut for the beating of the bounds

features: a stone turned recently in its socket
a threshold mark worn only at the edges
a gate shut in a fence with no fence
a court roll open at a penalty
a staff leaning by a door
scuff marks going the wrong way round

decisions.cue: a gate standing shut in a fence with no fence either side
decisions.cost: it can be opened or walked round

resolve.success: you open it properly and the village considers you to have come in the right way
resolve.failure: you walk round it and everything here treats you as having climbed in: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: open it wrong; it will not shut again behind you

decisions.cue: a moot stone with worn places where feet have stood
decisions.cost: standing in the place is a claim to be heard

resolve.success: you stand where the speaker stands and the Manor Court answers your question
resolve.failure: you stand in the wrong place and are held in contempt of a court you cannot see
resolve.orElse: stay off the stone; nothing here will hear you out

decisions.cue: a threshold mark worn only at the edges
decisions.cost: stepping over it is correct; standing on it is not

resolve.success: you step over it and pass unremarked
resolve.failure: you tread on it and everything indoors knows you are there
resolve.orElse: go round to another door, costing a Turn

decisions.cue: a staff cut for the beating of the bounds, leaning by a door
decisions.cost: carrying it makes you part of the procession

resolve.success: you take it up and can walk the bounds unhindered, in the right direction
resolve.failure: you carry it widdershins and the bounds close behind you: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: leave the staff; the bounds will not let you out where you came in

decisions.cue: a court roll listing every custom and the penalty for breaking it
decisions.cost: knowing the penalties is worth more than knowing the customs

resolve.success: you find the one custom nobody here has kept, and can hold them to it
resolve.failure: you read out a penalty and it is applied to you
resolve.orElse: leave the roll; you will break something without knowing

decisions.cue: a stone that is turned once a season by whoever is nearest
decisions.cost: turning it early or late both mean something

resolve.success: you turn it at the right season and the year here moves on, and the way clears
resolve.failure: you turn it wrongly and it is the wrong season now: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it unturned; the season here does not change and neither does anything else

situations.doing: sitting on the moot stone with nothing before it
situations.onArrival: it stops and looks up as though your case were next
situations.because: the court sits on this day and has always sat
situations.offer: state a case and it will find in your favour, and enforce it

situations.doing: walking the bounds in the wrong direction and stopping each time
situations.onArrival: it asks you which way round it goes
situations.because: somebody walked them backwards once and it has not recovered
situations.offer: tell it the right way and it will walk you out past anything

situations.doing: measuring a fence that runs between two fields of nothing
situations.onArrival: they ask whether you know where the boundary actually is
situations.because: the enclosure was never agreed and they were sent anyway
situations.offer: help them fix a line and they will show you where the stone is buried

situations.occupant: an old man of the Parish
situations.doing: turning a stone in its socket, back and forth, unable to stop
situations.onArrival: he asks what season it is
situations.because: he was told to turn it once and cannot remember whether he has
situations.offer: give him a season and the year here moves, and a door opens with it

situations.doing: standing shut in a fence with no fence either side
situations.onArrival: the latch lifts slightly as you approach
situations.because: it was hung to be opened in an order and the order was broken
situations.offer: open it in the right order and every other gate in the parish opens with it

situations.doing: standing in a ring on the green in silence
situations.onArrival: they open the ring on the side you approach from
situations.because: the court cannot rise until somebody speaks
situations.offer: speak, and be answered, and be bound by the answer

temptations.cue: a bounds-staff, worn smooth
temptations.benefit: once, walk through any boundary here
temptations.standingDrawback: you must finish the round you started

temptations.cue: the court roll
temptations.benefit: hold anyone here to a custom they have broken
temptations.standingDrawback: they can hold you to one too

temptations.cue: a chip off the boundary stone
temptations.benefit: once, decide where a line falls
temptations.standingDrawback: the line moves for everybody, not just you

temptations.cue: the gate keys, in order on a ring
temptations.benefit: once, open a way that was closed in the right order
temptations.standingDrawback: the order matters, and you will get it wrong eventually

temptations.cue: a threshold mark, cut into something portable
temptations.benefit: once, be treated as having come in correctly
temptations.standingDrawback: what you left behind came in incorrectly

quiet.dangerLine: everybody here agreed not to speak of it and they are all still keeping to it

institution: a village where conversation stops at a certain topic and starts again after it
a vestry that keeps two sets of minutes
a pest house nobody mentions and everybody avoids
ritual: a subject changed at the same point every time
a door pulled to before certain words
the same answer given by everyone to the same question
demand: a silence held open, waiting for you to fill it
a question asked twice and left the second time
a room that goes quiet as you come in and does not start again
wound: minutes with a week cut out of them
a name gone out of every mouth in one season
a pest house with the door barred from outside
anchor: the book nobody has read since it was written
the second set of minutes, complete
a witness who never agreed to the silence

features: a subject changed mid-sentence
minutes with a week cut out
a door pulled to as you pass
a barred door on an empty house
the same answer from three people
a silence that does not fill

decisions.cue: a room that goes quiet as you come in and does not start again
decisions.cost: the silence can be broken or joined

resolve.success: you wait it out and somebody breaks first, and tells you more than they meant to
resolve.failure: you fill the silence and are marked as somebody who talks: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave the room; the talk resumes behind you, about you

decisions.cue: vestry minutes with a week cut out of them and the stubs left
decisions.cost: the same week exists in the second set

resolve.success: you find the second minutes and read what the parish agreed to that week
resolve.failure: you are found with the minutes open at that week
resolve.orElse: leave them; the week stays missing, and so does the reason for everything

decisions.cue: a pest house with the door barred from the outside
decisions.cost: unbarring it is not undoing it

resolve.success: you open it and what is inside is grateful, and will name names
resolve.failure: you open it and what is inside was barred in for a reason: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: leave it barred; you will not learn what the village did

decisions.cue: the same answer given to the same question by three different people
decisions.cost: the fourth person is the one to ask

resolve.success: you find who has not learned the answer and they tell you the truth of it
resolve.failure: you press one of the three and the village closes to you entirely
resolve.orElse: stop asking; every route from here on is the hard one

decisions.cue: a name that has gone out of every mouth in one season
decisions.cost: saying it aloud will get a reaction

resolve.success: you say it to the right person alone and they break and tell you everything
resolve.failure: you say it in company and the whole village turns: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: never say it; the thing it names is not addressed at the ending

decisions.cue: a book nobody has read since it was written, still in its wrapping
decisions.cost: reading it is the breach the village was avoiding

resolve.success: you read it and know the transgression whole, and can name it at the ending
resolve.failure: you read it aloud and everything that agreed to the silence hears you
resolve.orElse: leave it wrapped; the ending has to be improvised without the truth

situations.doing: talking in a doorway and stopping at the same point
situations.onArrival: one of them changes the subject before you are close enough to hear
situations.because: the subject is changed at that point and always has been
situations.offer: let the subject stand changed and one of them will follow you out and tell you

situations.doing: copying minutes into a second book by candle
situations.onArrival: it turns the second book face down as you come in
situations.because: two sets have been kept since the week that is missing
situations.offer: promise not to say and it will let you read the true set

situations.doing: standing outside a barred door with no intention of opening it
situations.onArrival: they ask, flatly, whether you are here about that
situations.because: they were posted here and never relieved
situations.offer: tell them you are and they will hand over the bar and walk away

situations.occupant: an old woman of the Parish
situations.doing: answering a question nobody has asked her
situations.onArrival: she gives you the answer the village agreed on, word for word
situations.because: everybody was told what to say
situations.offer: ask her the question the answer does not fit and she will tell you the truth

situations.doing: mouthing a name without sound
situations.onArrival: it looks to see whether anyone else heard it
situations.because: it was told never to say the name and has not stopped saying it
situations.offer: say the name back and it will take you to where the thing happened

situations.doing: standing barred with the thatch fallen in
situations.onArrival: something inside stops moving when you stop walking
situations.because: it was barred from outside and never opened
situations.offer: speak to what is inside and it will answer, honestly, which nothing else here will

temptations.cue: the second set of vestry minutes
temptations.benefit: know what the parish agreed and when
temptations.standingDrawback: the parish knows you know

temptations.cue: the book nobody has read
temptations.benefit: once, name a truth that cannot be denied
temptations.standingDrawback: everything that agreed to the silence comes to stop you

temptations.cue: the bar off the pest house door
temptations.benefit: once, shut something in
temptations.standingDrawback: it was holding something shut and now is not

temptations.cue: the name nobody says
temptations.benefit: once, make anyone here answer you truthfully
temptations.standingDrawback: they resent it afterwards, and remember

temptations.cue: an agreement, given and taken
temptations.benefit: once, be unremarked anywhere in the parish
temptations.standingDrawback: you owe the silence back
